item.name: Auth - Google

request.description:
Expected: 200, returning the application's own `accessToken` / `refreshToken` (both in the body and as cookies).

Three resolution paths, in order:
1. **Known `googleId`** — resolved by the stable `sub` claim, never by email, because a Google email can change and `sub` cannot.
2. **Matching email on an existing account** — links it: sets `googleId`, forces `emailVerified: true`, and flips `authProvider` to `GOOGLE` *only* if the account had no password. An existing password is preserved. Role and status always come from the database, never from Google.
3. **New email** — provisions `User` (`role: PATIENT`, `password: null`, `authProvider: GOOGLE`, `emailVerified: true`, `image` from the `picture` claim) plus its `Patient` row in one transaction.

Account standing is checked on every path, including before the link-write, so a blocked or deleted account is refused without being mutated.

item.description:
ID-token verification only. The frontend runs Google Sign-In, gets an ID token, and POSTs it here; the server verifies it against `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID` and then issues **its own** JWTs. Google is never involved again after this one call — no client secret, no callback/redirect URL, no stored Google session.

See `GOOGLE-LOGIN-TESTING.md` in the repo for how to obtain a real ID token for the `googleIdToken` variable.

item.name: Auth

request.description:
Expected: **201**. In one Prisma transaction this creates a `User` (`role: PATIENT`, `status: ACTIVE`, `emailVerified: false`, `authProvider: CREDENTIALS`, bcrypt-hashed password) and its matching `Patient` row.

Returns `data: { accessToken, refreshToken, user, patient }`, and also sets both tokens as cookies. The test script stores the tokens in collection variables for the protected requests below.

There is no email verification step — the OTP/verify-email/forget-password/reset-password flows went away with better-auth.

Expected: 200 with `data: { accessToken, refreshToken, user }`.

Other outcomes from `AuthService.loginUser`:
- unknown email → 404 "User not found"
- `status: BLOCKED` → 403 "User is blocked"
- `isDeleted` or `status: DELETED` → 404 "User is deleted"
- account with no password (Google-only sign-in) → 400 "This account uses Google sign-in. Please continue with Google."
- wrong password → 401 "Invalid credentials"

item.description: All seven endpoints under `/api/v1/auth`. Protected routes (`/me`, `/change-password`, `/logout`) are gated by `checkAuth(ADMIN, DOCTOR, PATIENT, SUPER_ADMIN)` — every role passes, so the gate is really just "authenticated".
